title: Los Angeles students walk out to protest ICE immigration enforcement
seoTitle: Los Angeles student walkout against ICE

tea.why: Students are protesting against U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) raids and the Trump administration's immigration policies.
tea.want: Protesters are demanding an end to ICE enforcement actions and increased protections for undocumented families.
tea.changed: Nov 16: Thousands of students walked out of classes across Los Angeles to demonstrate at City Hall and other locations.

summary: On November 16, 2026, thousands of students from the Los Angeles Unified School District and surrounding areas walked out of their classrooms to protest U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) activities. Organized by South Central Community, the demonstration saw students from over 100 schools gather at Los Angeles City Hall and other local sites, such as Huntington Park City Hall. Participants carried signs and chanted slogans against federal immigration enforcement and the current administration's policies. While organizers promoted the event as a peaceful demonstration, reports noted a student burning an American flag during the gathering. The Los Angeles Unified School District stated that the walkouts were not school-sponsored events. Estimates regarding the number of participants varied, with a school police source citing over 7,000 students involved.
response: The Los Angeles Unified School District stated that the walkouts were not school-sponsored events and that students leaving without permission could be marked absent, though California law allows for certain excused absences for civic activities.

crowd.text: A school police source estimated that more than 7,000 students participated.

updates.text: Thousands of students walked out of classes to protest ICE, with many gathering at Los Angeles City Hall.
